Here comes the rush. Rodgers, pump, throw, lays it out there. Incomplete. Freiermuth had a step, but they could not complete it. He had that one to Metcalf in the second quarter.
Single running back is Warren. Warren breaks a tackle. They'll push him forward, just short of a first down. It's a gain of nine.

Motion man, Freiermuth. Fake it. Rodgers, looking, wide open, touchdown to Metcalf! The Steelers go back in front.

offense_strengths: Explosive deep passing game with accurate throws from Burrow to Chase, Higgins, and Gesicki for big gains and touchdowns
Effective use of play-action and RPO concepts leading to successful runs and passes
Versatile receivers like Chase who can be deployed anywhere and create after the catch
Ability to convert on third downs and sustain long drives with a mix of run and pass
defense_weaknesses: Susceptible to big runs by PIT backs like Warren (35+ yards)
Vulnerable in coverage to PIT tight ends and receivers on intermediate and deep routes leading to TDs
Missed opportunities on interceptions and allowing long pass plays (30+ yards)
Struggled to stop PIT's red zone efficiency and third down conversions

offense_strengths: Big play ability through deep shots and YAC from receivers like Wilson, Metcalf, Washington, and Skowronek for TDs
Effective play-action passes and quick hitters to TEs and RBs
Explosive runs by Warren (multiple 9+ yard gains and a 35-yard run)
Resilient in sustaining drives and capitalizing on turnovers and special teams opportunities
defense_weaknesses: Allowed multiple explosive passing plays and TDs to CIN receivers (Chase, Higgins, Gesicki)
Vulnerable to CIN's quick passes, screens, and YAC especially on short downs
Struggled containing Burrow's mobility and ability to extend plays
Gave up key third down conversions and long field goals
